name: Stuart Sutcliffe
milestone_by_age_26: Sold a painting to John Moores at the Walker Art Gallery's 1959 John Moores Painting Exhibition at age 19, and later enrolled as a master's student under Eduardo Paolozzi at the Hamburg State School of Art in 1961.
early_history_summary: Sutcliffe attended Liverpool College of Art where he met John Lennon and showed exceptional painting talent. His painting 'The Summer Painting' was selected for the John Moores Exhibition and purchased by John Moores himself for £65 in January 1960. He briefly joined the Beatles as bassist before leaving to pursue art in Hamburg under Eduardo Paolozzi.
primary_early_advantage_tags: art college, Lennon friendship, Paolozzi mentorship, Liverpool scene
evidence_summary: Sutcliffe showed early artistic talent at Liverpool College of Art, where he met John Lennon. His painting was purchased at the prestigious John Moores Exhibition at age 19, a significant achievement for a student. He briefly joined the Beatles before pursuing art under Eduardo Paolozzi at the Hamburg State School of Art. Family background is not well documented in reviewed sources.

name: Usain Bolt
milestone_by_age_26: Won 200m gold at the 2002 World Junior Championships at age 15, becoming the youngest-ever male world junior champion in athletics history.
early_history_summary: Bolt grew up in rural Sherwood Content, Jamaica, where his parents ran a local grocery store. He showed sprinting potential at Waldensia Primary School and was the school's fastest runner by age 12. His cricket coach at William Knibb Memorial High School steered him toward track and field, and he won gold at the 2002 World Junior Championships in Kingston at age 15.
family_context_summary: Bolt's parents, Wellesley and Jennifer Bolt, ran a local grocery store in the rural town of Sherwood Content, Jamaica. The family was of modest means.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; parents were grocers with no known athletics background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: physical talent, Jamaican sprint culture, high school coach, rural background
evidence_summary: Bolt grew up in rural Jamaica with grocer parents and showed exceptional sprinting speed from primary school. His high school coaches recognized his talent and steered him from cricket to track. At 15, he won the 2002 World Junior Championships 200m, becoming the youngest male world junior champion ever. Jamaica's deep sprint culture and high school athletics pipeline provided the ecosystem for his talent to emerge.

name: Dražen Petrović
milestone_by_age_26: Won the European Champions Cup (EuroLeague) with Cibona Zagreb in 1985 at age 21, and again in 1986, establishing himself as one of Europe's dominant basketball players.
early_history_summary: Petrović started playing basketball at age 13 with Šibenka's youth selections and made the senior first team at 15. He led Šibenka to two FIBA Korać Cup finals (1982, 1983) before joining Cibona Zagreb in 1984, where he won the European Champions Cup in 1985 and 1986. He and his brother Aleksandar practiced basketball every morning before school.
family_context_summary: Father Jovan was a police officer and mother Biserka was a librarian. The family was of modest means in Šibenik, Yugoslavia.
parent_family_domain_summary: Older brother Aleksandar was one of Yugoslavia's top point guards, providing direct basketball domain immersion and daily practice partnership from an early age.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Yugoslav basketball system, brother mentorship, early professional play, daily practice
evidence_summary: Petrović grew up in Šibenik, Croatia, with his father a police officer and mother a librarian. His older brother Aleksandar was already a top point guard, and the two practiced basketball every morning before school. Dražen joined Šibenka's senior team at 15 and led them to two European club competition finals. At Cibona Zagreb from 1984, he won back-to-back European Champions Cups at ages 21 and 22, cementing his status as one of Europe's best.

name: George Michael
milestone_by_age_26: Wham!'s debut album 'Fantastic' reached #1 on the UK Albums Chart in July 1983 when Michael was 20, following hit singles 'Young Guns (Go for It)' and 'Wham Rap!'
early_history_summary: Michael met Andrew Ridgeley at Bushey Meads School in the mid-1970s and they formed a ska band called the Executive in 1979. They formed Wham! in 1981 and were signed to Innervision Records in 1982. Their first single 'Wham Rap!' charted, and 'Young Guns (Go for It)' became a top-3 UK hit after a last-minute Top of the Pops performance. Their debut album 'Fantastic' went to #1 in the UK in 1983.
family_context_summary: Father was a Greek Cypriot restaurateur who immigrated to England in the 1950s; mother was an English dancer. The family was middle-class in Hertfordshire.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no known music industry family background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Ridgeley partnership, London pop scene, MTV era, songwriting talent
evidence_summary: Michael grew up in a Greek Cypriot family in north London and met Andrew Ridgeley at school. The pair formed bands from their mid-teens, persistently pursuing record deals. Wham! was signed in 1982 and their debut album reached #1 in the UK in 1983 when Michael was 20. The partnership with Ridgeley and the timing of the MTV-era British pop boom were key accelerants. Family financial background was modest middle-class.

name: Susan Polgár
milestone_by_age_26: Became the top-ranked female chess player in the world on FIDE's July 1984 rating list at age 15, and won the World Under-16 Girls Championship at age 12 in 1981.
early_history_summary: Susan Polgár was the eldest of three daughters in a deliberate educational experiment by her father László Polgár, who homeschooled all three with chess as the principal subject. Susan won the Budapest Girls' Under-11 Championship at age 4 with a perfect 10-0 score, the World Under-16 Girls Championship at 12, and became the world's top-rated female player at 15.
family_context_summary: Father László Polgár was a Hungarian teacher who designed a deliberate educational experiment to raise chess prodigies. Mother Klara assisted with homeschooling. All three daughters became chess champions.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father László Polgár was a teacher and chess educator who homeschooled all three daughters with chess as the principal subject, providing sustained individualized coaching from early childhood.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father's chess experiment, homeschooling, sibling practice, early tournament play, Hungarian chess tradition
evidence_summary: Susan Polgár was the eldest daughter of László Polgár, who conducted a deliberate educational experiment to prove that children could achieve exceptional results if trained intensively in a specialized subject from birth. All three daughters were homeschooled with chess as the principal subject. Susan won her first tournament at age 4, the World Under-16 Girls Championship at 12, and became the top-rated female player at 15. Her father's sustained coaching and the sibling practice environment were the dominant early advantages.

name: Ryuichi Sakamoto
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Yellow Magic Orchestra and released his debut solo album 'Thousand Knives' in 1978 at age 26, both pioneering electronic music works that launched his international career.
early_history_summary: Sakamoto began piano at age 6 and composition at age 10, influenced by Bach and Debussy. He studied at the Tokyo National University of Fine Arts and Music, where he worked with computers and electronic music. He became an in-demand session musician in the mid-1970s, playing with major Japanese artists. In 1978, he co-founded YMO with Haruomi Hosono and Yukihiro Takahashi and released his solo debut 'Thousand Knives'.
family_context_summary: Father Kazuki Sakamoto was a well-known literary editor who helped establish postwar Japanese literature by editing works of Mishima Yukio and Noma Hiroshi. Mother Keiko designed women's hats.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a prominent literary editor, providing a cultured intellectual environment though not directly a music domain advantage.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Tokyo University of Arts, electronic music frontier, YMO trio, session musician career, literary family
evidence_summary: Sakamoto began piano at 6 and composition at 10, studied at the elite Tokyo National University of Fine Arts and Music, and became an in-demand session musician in Tokyo's music scene. His father was a well-known literary editor who provided a cultured environment. In 1978 at age 26, he co-founded Yellow Magic Orchestra with two veteran musicians and released his pioneering solo electronic album 'Thousand Knives.' Tokyo's position at the frontier of electronic music and his elite institutional training were key accelerants.

name: Françoise Barré-Sinoussi
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Barré-Sinoussi completed her PhD in 1974 at age 27 and her Nobel-winning HIV discovery came in 1983 at age 36.

name: Phil Collins
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Genesis as drummer in August 1970 at age 19, recording multiple albums including 'Nursery Cryme' (1971), 'Foxtrot' (1972), and 'Selling England by the Pound' (1973), and became lead vocalist in 1975 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Collins began playing drums at age 5 and attended the Barbara Speake Stage School, where he acted as the Artful Dodger in the West End production of Oliver!. He played in several bands through his teens, including Flaming Youth who released the album 'Ark 2' in 1969. He auditioned for Genesis in 1970 after seeing an ad in Melody Maker and joined as their drummer at age 19.
family_context_summary: Father Greville was an insurance agent; mother June was a theatrical agent who previously worked in a toy shop. The family was middle-class in west London.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother worked as a theatrical agent at the Barbara Speake Stage School, which provided direct access to performing arts training and early acting roles.
primary_early_advantage_tags: stage school, London music scene, early drumming, mother's theater connections, Genesis
evidence_summary: Collins began drumming at age 5 and was enrolled at the Barbara Speake Stage School by his mother, a theatrical agent, which led to West End roles including the Artful Dodger in Oliver!. He played in multiple bands through his teens and joined Genesis as drummer at 19 in 1970. His mother's entertainment industry connections and London's music ecosystem were early accelerants, combined with exceptional drumming skill developed over 14 years.

name: Jacques Laffite
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Laffite came to motor racing late, attending the Winfield Racing School at age 25 in 1968/69. His first major achievements (Formule France 1972, French F3 title 1973, F1 debut 1974) all came after age 28.

name: Patrick Depailler
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Depailler's F1 debut was at the 1972 French Grand Prix at age 27, and his first major F2 results also came in 1972. No documented racing achievements before age 26.

name: Wladimir Klitschko
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold medal in super-heavyweight boxing at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics at age 20, and won the WBO heavyweight championship in 2000 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Klitschko followed his older brother Vitali into amateur boxing, training at the Brovary Olympic Reserve School in the late 1980s. He won gold at the Junior European Championships in 1993 at age 17, silver at the Junior World Championships in 1994, and Olympic gold in 1996 before turning professional. He won the WBO heavyweight title in 2000 at age 24.
family_context_summary: Father was a Soviet military officer. Older brother Vitali Klitschko became a multiple-time heavyweight world champion and later mayor of Kyiv.
parent_family_domain_summary: Older brother Vitali was already a competitive boxer who led Wladimir into the sport, providing direct domain immersion and a lifelong training partner.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Olympic reserve school, brother Vitali, Ukrainian boxing system, physical attributes
evidence_summary: Klitschko followed his older brother Vitali into boxing, training at the Brovary Olympic Reserve School in Ukraine. He won Junior European gold at 17, Junior World silver at 18, and Olympic super-heavyweight gold at 20 in 1996. His brother Vitali, already a boxer, provided domain immersion and a high-trust training partner. The Soviet/Ukrainian Olympic boxing pipeline and his exceptional physical attributes (6'6") were key accelerants.

name: Brad Pitt
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Pitt's breakthrough role was in 'Thelma & Louise' (1991) at age 27. Before 26, he had only uncredited film parts, TV guest roles, and minor film appearances.
